title: [CUDA] Add post-facto memory annotation API for memory snapshots
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #190575

The existing user-metadata mechanism (_set_memory_metadata) only stamps
metadata onto trace events as they are generated, so there is no way to
attach information to an allocation after the fact. That information is
often only available later, e.g. recording that a tensor is retained by
the autograd graph happens when it is packed into the tape, long after
the allocation.

This adds torch.cuda.memory._annotate_memory(data_ptr, metadata), which
records a new "annotate" trace action (TraceEntry::ANNOTATE) keyed to
the live allocation's base address, resolved via get_allocated_block
(raising on dead/unknown pointers), plus a tensor-level convenience
wrapper _annotate_tensor(tensor, metadata) that annotates the base of
the tensor's untyped storage so views and offset tensors just work.
Annotations are separate, timestamped trace events, so alloc-time
user_metadata is never clobbered and multiple annotations accumulate;
each also captures the annotation-site stack trace subject to the
record-history context setting. Alternatives considered: mutating the
ALLOC entry's user_metadata in the ring buffer (entry may already be
evicted, and string concatenation entangles the original metadata) or
storing annotations on the Block (lost on free, invisible in the
timeline); the trace-event approach avoids both problems.

Review order: the enum + parser in c10/core/CachingDeviceAllocator.h;
the allocator API in c10/cuda/CUDACachingAllocator.{h,cpp} (record_trace
gains a metadata override so annotate events carry the annotation
instead of the thread-local metadata); the bindings and action-string
maps in torch/csrc/{cuda,xpu}; the Python helpers in
torch/cuda/memory.py; and finally the visualizer, where
process_alloc_data.js joins annotate events onto live alloc elements
("Annotations:" section in the timeline tooltip), MemoryViz.js shows
them on live blocks in the segment view (reset when an address is
reused), and _memory_viz.py's trace view prints "# annotate NAME: ...".

Test Plan:

New test test_memory_plots_annotate covers two annotations on one
allocation (addr, content, order), that alloc-time metadata is not
clobbered, that _annotate_tensor on a view resolves to the storage base
address, and that annotating a freed pointer raises.

```
python -m pytest test/test_cuda.py -k "snapshot or memory_history or metadata or annotate" -q
```

17 passed, 1 skipped on an H100. The JS path was additionally verified
by dumping a real snapshot containing an annotation and running
process_alloc_data on it under node, checking that exactly one element
renders the annotation string.

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude).
